unresolved_distinctions.question: What is the complete set of valid foundation/application splits of the modules in package/artifacts/modules.json — every assignment of all six modules to non-empty layer1/layer2 such that no layer1 module depends (per the dependency list) on a layer2 module — together with the method that produced it?
unresolved_distinctions.why_unresolved: The package supplies only the module list and dependency edges; no enumeration of valid splits exists anywhere in the evidence state, and completeness of any enumeration is exactly what the task demands.
unresolved_distinctions.required_evidence: A first complete candidate enumeration: an explicit list of all valid {layer1, layer2} splits (sorted module lists, sorted items) plus a stated method (e.g. systematic enumeration of dependency-closed subsets of the DAG), derived from modules.json.
admissibility_constraints: Must cover the full space: 'Completeness is the deliverable: a missed item is a wrong answer.'
Every split must assign each module to exactly one layer, both layers non-empty, and satisfy 'no module in layer1 depends on a module in layer2' where {from: a, to: b} means a depends on b.
Per E-A, the enumeration must be accompanied by its method.

unresolved_distinctions.question: What does a second complete enumeration of the same split space contain, when produced by a process that has no access to the first enumeration or to any of its intermediate work?
unresolved_distinctions.why_unresolved: No such independently originated enumeration exists yet, and by E-B's authorship/access condition it cannot be supplied by the process that produced (or has seen) the first enumeration.
unresolved_distinctions.required_evidence: A complete enumeration of all valid splits produced from modules.json alone by a causally separated process whose inputs demonstrably exclude the first enumeration and all of its intermediate work.
admissibility_constraints: Per E-B, the second enumeration must be 'produced without access to the first enumeration or any of its intermediate work'.
The producing process may (and must) see the raw task space — modules.json — but nothing derived from the first enumeration path.
It must be a complete enumeration of the same space, not a spot-check of the first answer.

unresolved_distinctions.question: What is the final merged answer — the union of both enumerations with every item found by only one of them flagged — and is the completeness claim supported by both enumerations?
unresolved_distinctions.why_unresolved: The merge cannot exist until both enumerations exist; per E-C the completeness claim is admissible only when supported by both, so no completeness verdict is currently possible.
unresolved_distinctions.required_evidence: A merged result.json listing the union of the two enumerations (sorted), with any single-source item flagged, and a complete field justified by agreement of both enumerations (or PENDING-INTEGRATION / false otherwise).
admissibility_constraints: Per E-C, 'the completeness claim is admissible only when supported by both enumerations'.
Items found by only one enumeration must be flagged in the merged answer.
The merge presupposes that the second enumeration satisfies E-B's independence condition; a merge over two same-origin enumerations does not license the completeness claim.
